title: Resolve the effective device before capability caching or CUDA stream dispatch
applies_when: A capability, current_stream or kernel-dispatch helper defaults to the current accelerator, especially when tensors may be on a noncurrent device or the current device can change.
lesson: First establish whether a supported caller can change the current device or pass a noncurrent-device tensor; a hypothetical arbitrary device switch is not production reachability. A no-argument cache stores the first current-device answer, not a device-independent fact. Resolve the actual device index before the per-device cache and route tensor-dependent dispatch from the tensor's device when that caller contract permits it. Test both switch orders with differing capabilities, explicit-device calls, cache reuse and the non-CUDA fallback. CUDA current-stream state is also per device: current_stream() queries the process's current device, not the input tensor's device. Use distinct nondefault streams on two devices to expose that mismatch; default stream handles alone can hide it. Check same-device and explicit-stream controls and record the backend's device_id with the stream. A mocked query or intercepted launch can establish selection semantics; keep native operator qualification separate.
avoid_when: A one-device-per-rank worker can deliberately set its current device before model construction and use no-argument stream queries throughout that rank. TP across processes alone does not establish a noncurrent-device call. Inspect initialization and actual consumers before proposing a fix; changing one stream argument may leave current-device native allocations or graph capture inconsistent. Even homogeneous GPUs can have different current streams. A stable CUDA ordinal is a process-local identity, not a portable hardware profile or live resource allocation. Simulated capability queries do not prove mixed-hardware execution, PDL compatibility or performance. Real Torch stream selection with the final backend call intercepted is not TileLang kernel numerical or launch-context qualification. A device-scoped query alone does not establish that the native context, allocations and kernel handles agree. Preserve explicit caller streams; CPU, no-tensor and mixed-device input paths need their own contracts.

evidence.note: The original supports_pdl has a no-argument lru_cache and queries the current CUDA device, exposing the stale-answer mechanism after a device switch.

Proposed, unmerged fix includes seven CPU regressions using the real standalone utility module with mocked backend/device queries. Tests cover both switch orders, explicit device indices, property-cache reuse and non-CUDA fallback. They are not native mixed-GPU or operator performance evidence.
The exact Torch API documents device=None as the current CUDA device and passes the resolved device index to _cuda_getCurrentStream; it does not infer a tensor device.

Contributor-tested exact PR wrapper methods on two RTX5090s with Torch2.11 native tensors/streams: both noncurrent-device cases select the other device's stream; same-device, explicit-stream and device-scoped controls agree. Final backend calls were intercepted. No compiled TileLang kernel, numerical qualification, full current-main build or author acceptance is claimed.

This worker resolves its local visible GPU and sets the accelerator current device before distributed initialization. It supplies a concrete current-device-affinity precondition, not proof that all later extensions or calls preserve it.

The mono integration documents and caches one runner per TP rank, passes its device into DSV41MonoLayer and uses rank-local collective peer memory. TP is not evidence that a supported call changes the current device inside that process. Pinned-source countercondition only; no native AMD execution or blanket no-bug verdict.

The stream helper changes the device before saving previous_stream. That saved stream therefore belongs to the target device; resetting it alone does not establish restoration of the caller device. Inspect the actual decoder-slot producer and both device streams on normal/error exit, not an arbitrary fake backend. Source mechanism only; no codec, model or general backend qualification is asserted here.

Torch provides its own CUDA stream-selection context. Prefer checking the installed implementation's entry/exit behavior before maintaining a separate device/stream restoration stack. This API reference does not establish that every codec, dependency version or graph-capture use is compatible.
